method: Targeted evidence synthesis, not a preregistered exhaustive systematic review. Primary papers, author/institution repositories, syntheses, official platform guidance and one explicitly labeled practitioner account. Search snippets used only when identifiable as author/publisher material; access depth recorded. No full copyrighted papers redistributed.
interpretation: Study quality and relevance to math Shorts are separate. Effect sizes are study summaries, not additive gains or predicted channel lift. Proposed design rules require calibration.

sources.title: Multimedia Design for Learning: An Overview of Reviews With Meta-Meta-Analysis
sources.finding: 29 reviews encompassing 1,189 studies and 78,177 participants; positive effects for multiple design principles.
sources.limits: Broad instructional multimedia, not specifically feed-based math videos; overlapping syntheses are not independent replications.

sources.title: Improving instructional video design: A systematic review
sources.finding: 113 papers, 28 principles; coherence, segmentation and learner control supported across video contexts; modality and redundancy not supported as general video rules.
sources.limits: Heterogeneous methods; no dependable universal timing threshold or ranking of principles.

sources.title: How Video Production Affects Student Engagement
sources.finding: 6.9 million watching sessions in four edX courses; shorter videos and certain presentation styles associated with greater engagement.
sources.limits: MOOC engagement proxies, observational confounding, older desktop context; not proof of a six-minute cognitive limit or optimal Shorts length.

sources.title: States of Curiosity Modulate Hippocampus-Dependent Learning
sources.finding: High-curiosity states associated with better immediate and next-day memory for trivia answers and incidental information.
sources.limits: Laboratory trivia and memory, not a causal test of video hooks, virality or a dopamine-based editing recipe.

sources.title: What Is Interesting? Exploring the Appraisal Structure of Interest
sources.finding: Interest modeled through novelty/complexity and perceived capacity to understand.
sources.limits: Stimuli and appraisals differ from mathematical Shorts; neither universal optimal complexity nor cut timing established.

sources.title: Saying the wrong thing: improving learning with multimedia by including misconceptions
sources.finding: 364 first-year physics students; misconception refutation and dialogue produced greater conceptual gains than concise exposition in this experiment.
sources.limits: Physics instruction and pre/post conceptual tests; not evidence that misleading hooks or prolonged confusion improve feed retention.

sources.title: When Problem Solving Followed by Instruction Works
sources.access: publisher excerpts and author abstract in ERIC
sources.finding: 53 studies, 166 comparisons; overall g=0.36 favoring problem solving before instruction, with implementation-dependent outcomes.
sources.limits: Structured problem-solving and consolidation; a brief rhetorical question is not the same intervention.

sources.title: Understanding Difficulties and Resulting Confusion in Learning
sources.finding: Confusion may support learning when resolved with suitable guidance; persistent unresolved confusion can become frustration or boredom.
sources.limits: Effects depend on prior knowledge, task and support. Deliberately obscuring an explanation is not justified.

sources.title: Instructional animation versus static pictures: A meta-analysis
sources.finding: 26 studies, 76 comparisons; overall d=0.37 favoring animation, with variation by representational purpose and task.
sources.limits: Moderators can co-vary; this does not prescribe photorealism for abstract mathematics.

sources.title: Does animation enhance learning? A meta-analysis
sources.finding: 61 experiments, 140 comparisons, 7,036 participants; overall animation benefit but most individual comparisons not statistically significant.
sources.limits: Animation is conditional, not automatically superior to a well-designed static display.

sources.title: Animation: can it facilitate?
sources.finding: Graphics should match the concept and remain perceivable and interpretable; transient motion can undermine comprehension.
sources.limits: Foundational theory, not an experimentally validated Shorts production specification.

sources.title: Learning Versus Performance: An Integrative Review
sources.finding: Immediate performance and subjective fluency can diverge from durable retention and transfer.
sources.limits: Watching time, confidence and immediate quizzes alone cannot establish long-term learning.

sources.title: Interpolated memory tests reduce mind wandering and improve learning of online lectures
sources.finding: Tests between lecture segments reduced mind wandering and improved learning in the studied online lecture setting.
sources.limits: Roughly 22-minute lecture with actual responses; silent prediction in a Short is a proposed adaptation.

sources.title: Inducing Self-Explanation: A Meta-Analysis
sources.finding: 69 effects from 64 reports; mean g=0.55 for self-explanation prompts.
sources.limits: Learners actually generated explanations; merely showing a prompt does not demonstrate participation.

sources.title: Using narratives and storytelling to communicate science with nonexpert audiences
sources.finding: Narrative organizes causality, events and characters; can engage nonexperts but also gives individual examples persuasive force.
sources.limits: Narrative is not evidence of a general theorem; salient anecdotes can distort statistical understanding.

sources.title: What Makes Online Content Viral?
sources.finding: Emotional activation associated with sharing in news data, with experimental support for effects on transmission.
sources.limits: News/email and experimental transmission are not math Shorts retention or learning; emotion types are not interchangeable.

sources.title: How effective is emotional design?
sources.finding: Pleasant colors and/or anthropomorphic instructional graphics showed learning benefits; affective mediation was less settled.
sources.limits: Specific design manipulations; no universal best palette, mascot or rationale for unrelated decoration.

sources.title: Keep It Coherent: A Meta-Analysis of the Seductive Details Effect
sources.finding: Interesting irrelevant details can impair learning; effects vary by material and methodology.
sources.limits: Does not imply every beautiful, humorous or emotionally meaningful element is irrelevant.

sources.title: Intuitions about mathematical beauty
sources.finding: Laypeople made systematic aesthetic judgments of simple mathematical arguments; elegance, profundity and clarity related to judgments.
sources.limits: Selected arguments and judgments, not evidence of universal taste or increased watch time.

sources.title: The Four-Phase Model of Interest Development
sources.finding: Distinguishes triggered and maintained situational interest from developing individual interest.
sources.limits: A framework for development, not a validated subscriber conversion model.

sources.title: When scientists ’Tok
sources.finding: 1,025 science TikToks from 113 creators; humor and imitation positively associated with engagement metrics in multilevel models.
sources.limits: Associations, not causal effects; no comprehension test and no proof that adding memes improves mathematics learning.

sources.citation: Facilitating knowledge construction in informal learning (2023)
sources.title: A study of TikTok scientific, educational videos
sources.finding: 114 videos and 259,508 comments; most comments social; informational content, original audio and analytic language associated with more knowledge-related discussion.
sources.limits: Classifier labels and commenter self-selection; discussion is not representative viewer learning.

sources.title: Making Science Education More Accessible
sources.finding: Analysis of 150 sampled science TikToks explores associations among video characteristics and engagement.
sources.limits: Successful single creator; selection and platform effects limit generalization.

sources.title: Designing and Evaluating LLM-Generated Short-Form Educational Videos
sources.finding: 62 university students, introductory programming; structured generated reels improved immediate quizzes and efficiency relative to selected longer videos.
sources.limits: Bundle of format/content changes; brief quiz, limited population, no durable-learning test. Do not infer a pure duration effect.

sources.title: PaperTok: Exploring the Use of Generative AI for Creating Short-form Videos for Research Communication
sources.access: full text sections; DOI listed in manuscript
sources.finding: Formative N=8, researchers N=18 and audience N=100; tested an iterative AI authoring system, highlighting perceived engagement and demand for granular control.
sources.limits: Comparisons with other generation tools; perceived informational value is not measured mathematical transfer.

sources.title: Educational Short Videos: Bibliometric Trends, Thematic Structure, and Operationalisation
sources.finding: 2,169 indexed records through June 11, 2026; inconsistent operationalization of shortness and outcomes.
sources.limits: Maps the field rather than estimates causal effectiveness. Preprint status.

sources.title: Search and discovery tips — Shorts
sources.finding: Ranking uses watch choice, viewing duration/percentage and satisfaction signals, with personalization and competition.
sources.limits: No public universal winning threshold, exact weighting or guarantee of distribution.

sources.title: Understand your YouTube content performance
sources.finding: Shorts average duration and percentage viewed use engaged views and corresponding watch time.
sources.limits: Denominators differ from all feed exposures; do not equate completion among stayers with reach or understanding.

sources.title: Background Music and Cognitive Task Performance
sources.finding: Music effects depend on tasks, music and populations; lyrics and demanding tasks can be problematic.
sources.limits: Cognitive-task performance is not the whole audiovisual entertainment experience.

sources.citation: de la Mora Velasco et al. (2023)
sources.title: The impact of background music on learners
sources.finding: 47 studies, 71 effects, overall d=0.314 favoring background music across heterogeneous learning settings.
sources.limits: Timing, tasks and music differ; does not establish that continuous music improves narrated mathematical explanations.

sources.title: A coherence effect in multimedia learning: The case for minimizing irrelevant sounds
sources.finding: Extraneous audio harmed some retention and transfer outcomes; sound-effect results varied across experiments.
sources.limits: Older software and particular sounds; not a ban on sparse, meaningful event sounds.

sources.title: How Soundtracks Shape What We See
sources.finding: N=118, alternative soundtracks for a film scene changed aspects of interpretation and perception.
sources.limits: Film emotion and character interpretation; no math-learning claim.

sources.title: Instructor enthusiasm in online lectures
sources.finding: Vocal enthusiasm increased reported engagement; second study increased intention to watch another lecture; no conclusive quiz benefit.
sources.limits: 22-minute university lecture; intentions are not actual returns. Null quiz result is not proof of zero effect.

sources.citation: I am Alexa, your virtual tutor! (2022)
sources.title: Text-to-speech voice enthusiasm in multimedia learning
sources.finding: Synthetic speech can convey emotional tone; investigated enthusiasm as a multimedia design feature.
sources.limits: Specific engine and setting; cannot rank current local TTS systems or validate present-day voice quality.

sources.title: The Attentional Theory of Cinematic Continuity
sources.access: author repository abstract and manuscript excerpts
sources.finding: Attention and perceptual expectations help explain continuity across cuts.
sources.limits: Film theory informs a design analogy; no fixed edit rate established for mathematics.

sources.title: The Recall and Recognition of Sonic Logos
sources.finding: 90 sonic logos, N=1,860; recognition and sung recall reflect different aspects of melodic structure.
sources.limits: Sonic-logo memory is not channel loyalty; best signature must be tested in context.

sources.title: Understanding Captions (Prerecorded)
sources.finding: Synchronized captions make spoken and meaningful non-speech audio accessible.
sources.limits: Accessibility rationale, not an empirical engagement optimization study.

sources.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
sources.finding: Documents position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases in model judging alongside useful agreement in studied tasks.
sources.limits: Chat-response judgments do not validate simulated human responses to audiovisual entertainment.

sources.citation: Take caution in using LLMs as human surrogates (2025)
sources.title: Human-surrogate validation research
sources.finding: Compares model response distributions with human data and identifies limits to substitution.
sources.limits: Specific tasks and models; supports calibration requirements rather than claims about all future models.

sources.title: SoME1 results
sources.finding: Highlights motivation, clarity, topic selection and non-obvious insights in mathematical exposition.
sources.limits: Expert creative judgment and selected examples; not a controlled test of causal effectiveness.

sources.title: Understand three-minute YouTube Shorts
sources.finding: Current square/vertical Shorts limit is 180 seconds. Over-one-minute Shorts with active copyright claims are blocked.
sources.limits: Platform constraint, not an optimal educational duration; recheck when publishing.
